turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

I grouped the 300 training rows into chemical families and looked at where the high zT(400 K) values sit:

**High-zT families (target > 0.4):**

| Family | Training examples | target |
|---|---|---|
| Sb–Te–Ag / Sb–Ag (AgSbTe₂-like) | Sb0.25/Te0.50/Ag0.25 | 0.75–0.90 |
| Sb–Mg–Ag / Sb–Mg–Bi (Mg₃Sb₂) | Sb0.29/Mg0.60/Bi0.10 | 0.28–0.79 |
| **PbTe (Te≈0.50, Pb≈0.45–0.50)** | Te0.5/Pb0.4525 → **0.78**; +Cu → 0.60 | 0.20–0.78 |
| **Sb-doped Mg₂(Si,Sn), Sn-rich** | Mg0.67/Sn0.19/Si0.13 + Sb 0.002–0.008 | 0.50–0.57 (rises with Sb) |
| **Mg₂Sn-rich (Sn ≥ 0.25)** | Mg0.67/Sn0.25/Ge0.08 → 0.66; Mg0.68/Sn0.17/Si0.14 → 0.65 | 0.46–0.66 |
| **Sn-only (β-Sn ≈ 0.556)** | Sn0.5556 → **0.71** | 0.71 |
| CoSb₃ skutterudites, In-filled | Sb0.72/Co0.24/In0.018 → **0.70**; unfilled → 0.29–0.44 | 0.28–0.70 |
| Se–Pb, Pb–S(+Cu) | Se0.50/Pb0.49/Cu0.014 → 0.56; Pb0.50/S0.50/Cu0.005 → 0.47 | 0.15–0.56 |

**Low-zT families:** anything oxide-rich (O > 0.2) is essentially always < 0.07; Si-rich or Cu₂Se/Cu₂S-rich, Te–Cu, In–Se, half-Heusler Ti/Zr–Ni–Sn, S-based sulfides are all mostly < 0.2.

**Screening the pool against these motifs:**

- **c049** — Sb0.023/Mg0.669/Sn0.185/Si0.123: exactly the Sb-doped Mg₂Si₀.₄Sn₀.₆ family whose members give 0.50–0.57, and its Sb doping level is the highest of that group (trend is increasing with Sb) → est. ≈0.6.
- **c046** — Mg0.66/Sn0.267/Si0.067: the Sn-richest Mg₂(Si,Sn) in the pool; nearest analogues 0.65–0.66 → est. ≈0.6.
- **c037** — Te0.50/Pb0.45: nearest neighbour in training is Te0.5/Pb0.4525 = **0.78** (Pb-deficient PbTe is the best of the PbTe set) → est. ≈0.6 (high upside).
- **c010** — Sn0.558: essentially identical to the Sn0.5556 sample at **0.71** → est. ≈0.7 (one-sample support, but exact match).
- **c096** — Sb0.735/Co0.245/In0.0061: In-filled CoSb₃; the In-filled training sample is the best skutterudite (0.70), unfilled ones 0.29–0.44 → est. ≈0.5.
- Runners-up: c043/c054 (Sb–Mg–Bi, 0.28–0.79 spread), c018 (PbS+Cu ≈0.46), c055/c091 (PbTe+Cu ≈0.4), c064/c087 (Te-doped CoSb₃ ≈0.35).
- Rejected: all O-rich (c006, c017, c029, c041, c045, c048, c066, c073, c083, c093, c094), Si/Cu/Ni-rich (c012, c024, c042, c077), In–Se (c067), sulfides and half-Heuslers (c021, c022, c036, c079, c090).

**Final: c010, c037, c049, c046, c096**
